title: Exact localization preserves the specified inverse mate
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal D,\mathcal F$ be abelian categories with chosen ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $L_1:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $R_1:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$, $L_2:\mathcal D\to\mathcal F$, $R_2:\mathcal F\to\mathcal D$, $G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal D$ and $H:\mathcal B\to\mathcal F$ be additive exact functors. Fix adjunctions $a_1:L_1\dashv R_1$, $a_2:L_2\dashv R_2$, and an isomorphism $d:GR_1\xrightarrow{\sim}R_2H$. Let $\beta:L_2G\to HL_1$ be its inverse mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], and assume $\beta$ invertible. Give $D(L_i)\dashv D(R_i)$ the exact localized adjunctions of [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction]. Use the standard exact-composition isomorphisms to form $D(d):D(G)D(R_1)\cong D(R_2)D(H)$. Its inverse mate $\beta^D$ is precisely $D(\beta)$ under those isomorphisms, and is therefore invertible. This assertion concerns these specified localized adjunctions, including their Hom bijections: for complexes $K,L$, the exact-functor factorization isomorphisms carry the localized adjunct of a cochain map $L_1K\to L$ to the localization of its ordinary cochain adjunct. Writing $\varphi_{F,K}:D(F)Q(K)\cong Q(F^\#K)$ for the exact-functor factorization and $a_i^\#$ for the degreewise cochain adjunction, the Hom normalization is $\operatorname{adj}_{D(a_i)}(Q(f)\circ\varphi_{L_i,K})=\varphi_{R_i,L}^{-1}\circ Q(\operatorname{adj}_{a_i^\#}(f))$. The mate equality holds on all derived objects; no faithfulness of localization is assumed.

proof.text: For every exact functor T, use [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to obtain the standard factorization φ_T of D(T)Q through the termwise cochain functor. The composition and natural-isomorphism lifting formulas from [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] show that the standard derived square associated to e, conjugated by the two successive factorization isomorphisms on each side, equals Q applied to its cochain square. In Lean, square_fac proves this using mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_fac, mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fac, naturality, and cancellation of inverse isomorphisms.

proof.text: The cochain adjunction $a^\#:L^\#\dashv R^\#$ is degreewise the given adjunction $a:L\dashv R$ of [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction]. Explicitly, the adjunct of $f:L^\#K\to N$ is $g=R^\#(f)\circ\eta^\#_K$ and its inverse sends $g$ to $\varepsilon^\#_N\circ L^\#(g)$. Naturality of $\eta$ and $\varepsilon$ makes these families commute with the differentials; the two composites are identities by the triangle identities in each degree. Thus these are actual cochain maps and the stated cochain Hom bijection.

proof.text:
For either specified localized adjunction of [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction], its localized unit and counit give
$\eta^D_{QK}=\chi_{R,L,K}^{-1}Q(\eta^\#_K)$ and
$\varepsilon^D_{QN}=Q(\varepsilon^\#_N)\chi_{L,R,N}$.
These follow by applying the transformation-lifting formula of step 1 to the original unit and counit; their source or target identity functor has identity factorization. For $f:L^\#K\to N$, expand the adjunct as $D(R)(Q(f)\varphi_{L,K})\eta^D_{QK}$. Substituting the unit formula cancels $D(R)(\varphi_{L,K})$ against its inverse and leaves
$D(R)(Qf)\varphi_{R,L^\#K}^{-1}Q(\eta^\#_K)
=\varphi_{R,N}^{-1}Q(R^\#f)Q(\eta^\#_K)
=\varphi_{R,N}^{-1}Q(\operatorname{adj}_{a^\#}(f))$.
The first equality is precisely naturality of $\varphi_R$ at $f$; the last is step 2. This proves the requested Hom normalization for the specified adjunctions.

proof.text: For a pair of adjunctions and the square d of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], characterize its inverse mate β by the unit equation η₂ at GK followed by R₂(β_K) = G(η₁ at K) followed by d at L₁K. This is unit_mateEquiv_symm. The equation determines β: the second adjunction Hom bijection sends β_K to its left side and is injective. Applying the original unit equation degreewise gives an equality of actual cochain maps by extensionality in each degree.

proof.text: Localize the unit equation from step 4 using the specified adjunctions [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction]. On QK, precompose by φ_G inverse and postcompose by the successive H,L₁,R₂ factorization maps; all these maps are isomorphisms. For its left side, naturality of the second localized unit, the localized unit formula of step 3, and square_fac of step 1 for β reduce the composite to Q of η₂# followed by R₂# of the cochain β square. For its right side, the first localized unit formula, naturality of φ_G inverse and of D(d), and square_fac for d reduce it to Q of G#η₁# followed by the cochain d square. Their equality is the degreewise unit equation of step 4. Thus D(β), with the standard composition identifications, satisfies the localized unit equation at every QK. This is the direct cochain calculation mate_unit_Q; it uses only exactness and no tensor or resolution hypotheses.

proof.text: At QK, unit_mateEquiv_symm says that the inverse mate of D(d) satisfies the same localized unit equation. Apply injectivity of the second localized adjunction Hom bijection and step 5 to identify the two components. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](3), Localization.natTrans_ext extends their equality to all derived objects, without assuming Q faithful. The derived square of the ordinary isomorphism β is an isomorphism, so the equality gives IsIso of the localized inverse mate. Combine this with both Hom normalizations from step 3.

The statement is byte-identical to the base (all 294 earlier snapshots hold it unsplit), and live and side-live still show it unsplit. There is no repair note, no SGA citation and no supersession. Statement check: β is the inverse mate of d with the correct direction (def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate). The Hom normalization type-checks, and β being invertible is a separate hypothesis. Tested on zero categories, the identity square, a scalar automorphism (stays u, not u⁻¹) and a non-invertible unit. Step 1 uses the exact-functor factorization leaf (mapDerivedCategoryFactors) and clause (2) of the localization leaf (liftNatTrans); χ is the composite of the φ maps. Step 2 checks the cochain adjunction degreewise. In step 3 I recomputed η^D = χ⁻¹Q(η#) and ε^D = Q(ε#)χ from def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction, and the Hom clause follows by naturality of φ_R at f. Step 4 applies the inverse-mate formula degreewise, using d and not d⁻¹. In step 5 I checked the three arrows under the χ/φ identifications, which give β^D_QK = χ_{H,L1}⁻¹Q(β#)χ_{L2,G}. Step 6 uses clause (3) of the localization leaf (natTrans_ext) for equality on all objects, not faithfulness of Q, and clause (2) for the inverse. Sources: Stacks 07A7 remark-base-change (sites-cohomology.tex l.4033) and the units/counits sentence of blueprint main-20261015 fix-prop-coherence.proof.md, both read.
